items.stem: A duck floats on a pond. A wave passes underneath. What happens to the duck?

options.text: The duck rides the wave to the other side of the pond
The duck bobs up and down, mostly staying in the same place
The duck sinks until the wave passes
The duck is pushed sideways by the moving water

items.explanation: The wave carries energy across the pond, but the water itself (and the duck on top of it) mostly stays put. The duck only rises and falls.

items.stem: When a wave travels across the ocean, what is actually moving from one place to another?

options.text: Water molecules, traveling all the way to shore
Energy, while the water mostly stays in place
Air, pushed by the wind
Both energy and water, in equal amounts

items.explanation: Waves transfer energy without transporting matter. The water particles vibrate up and down, but the energy is what travels across the ocean.

items.stem: Two astronauts float in space inches apart. One shouts. Why can't the other one hear it?

options.text: Their helmets block all sound
Sound is an electromagnetic wave and travels too slowly
Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a medium, there's no air in space
Sound only works for distances under a meter

items.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave, so it needs a medium (like air) to travel through. Space is a vacuum, no medium, no sound.

items.stem: Which of the following can travel through completely empty space?

options.text: Sound waves from a speaker
Ocean waves
Visible light from the Sun
A stadium wave

items.explanation: Visible light is an electromagnetic wave; it doesn't need a medium. That's why sunlight can cross 93 million miles of empty space to reach Earth in about 8 minutes.

items.stem: Look at the wave below. Which letter points to the trough?

options.text: Point A, the highest part of the wave
Point B, the calm middle line
Point C, the lowest part of the wave
Point D, somewhere between the peak and the line

items.explanation: Point C is at the very bottom of a dip, that's the trough. Point A marks a crest (highest point), B sits on the resting line, and D is somewhere between.

items.stem: What is the resting position of a wave?

options.text: The peak of the wave
The point where the wave stops moving
The calm middle line that the wave rises above and dips below
The same thing as the wavelength

items.explanation: The resting position is the level the wave would sit at if it weren't moving. Crests rise above it, troughs dip below it.

items.stem: Wave X has peaks that are very close together. Wave Y has peaks that are far apart. What can you say about their wavelengths?

options.text: Wave X has a longer wavelength than Wave Y
Wave X has a shorter wavelength than Wave Y
Both waves have the same wavelength
You need to know the heights to compare wavelengths

items.explanation: Wavelength is the distance from one peak to the next. Peaks close together = short wavelength. Peaks far apart = long wavelength. The height (amplitude) doesn't matter, wavelength is measured side-to-side.

items.stem: What does the frequency of a wave tell you?

options.text: How tall the wave is
How far apart the peaks are
How many crests pass a point each second
How fast the wave is moving

items.explanation: Frequency counts how many wave crests pass a fixed point in one second. It's measured in Hertz (Hz). It's about how often something happens, not how the wave looks.

items.stem: Compare these two waves. Wave X and Wave Y have the same wavelength but different heights. What does that tell you?

options.text: Wave X has a higher frequency than Wave Y
Wave X carries more energy than Wave Y
Wave Y carries more energy than Wave X
Both waves carry the same amount of energy

items.explanation: Wave Y has a much larger amplitude, and larger amplitude means more energy. The wavelengths are identical, so frequency is the same; only the amplitude (and therefore the energy) differs.

items.stem: If an electromagnetic wave has a shorter wavelength than another, what else is true about it?

options.text: It has a lower frequency and less energy
It has a higher frequency and more energy
Its frequency stays the same
It has a smaller amplitude

items.explanation: Wavelength and frequency are inversely linked. Shorter wavelength means more crests pass each second, higher frequency. For EM waves, higher frequency also means more energy. That's why gamma rays (very short wavelength) carry far more energy than radio waves (very long wavelength).
